Download Presentation Flight Plan Interactive What You Submit Back to Unit 3 Mission Focus You can revise a rocket assembly using fit-check evidence before fabrication. Revise Document Prepare Use the required lesson evidence to demonstrate this standard: The revision addresses a documented issue and the repeated check shows whether it improved the assembly. Mission Briefing Today’s Plan Use this page with the lesson presentation, your engineering notebook, and the tools or evidence assigned for Resolve Assembly Issues Before Printing. Learning Targets Review assembly evidence for unresolved fit or alignment issues. Make targeted revisions rather than random changes. Document what changed and why it changed. Success Looks Like You can revise a rocket assembly using fit-check evidence before fabrication. Launch Learn Apply Check Submit Opening Prompt How do engineers revise an assembly before printing? Connect your response to the decision, evidence, or quality standard required for Resolve Assembly Issues Before Printing. Reveal: useful engineering move This lesson is ready to move forward when the evidence meets this standard: The revision addresses a documented issue and the repeated check shows whether it improved the assembly. Core Skill What We Are Practicing Key Idea 1 Revision work should be driven by evidence. Key Idea 2 Before printing, the assembly should pass basic fit and alignment checks. Key Idea 3 Good revision notes prevent repeated mistakes. Your Task Resolve Assembly Issues Before Printing Use the assembly evidence collected so far to revise part placement, fit, or component geometry before files are submitted. Review the fit, joint, and symmetry checks. Prioritize one issue that could prevent successful assembly. Make the required model or assembly revision. Repeat the relevant check and document the result. Quality check: The revision addresses a documented issue and the repeated check shows whether it improved the assembly. Lesson Interactive Prioritize Assembly Revisions Identify which issues must be fixed before parts are exported and choose the first problem the team should resolve. Assembly Review Findings Select every issue that blocks printing Nose cone overlaps the body wall by 1.2 mm One fin is not controlled by a joint Coupler clearance is still 0.10 mm instead of 0.30 mm Body color does not match the team’s preferred render First Priority Which issue should be addressed first? Choose Physical interference Missing joint Incorrect clearance Color choice Check Revision Plan Fix geometry and fit problems before cosmetic appearance. Physical interference is the first priority. What You Will Submit Assembly Revision Evidence Before-and-after evidence for one assembly revision. A brief note connecting the change to the original issue. Submission standard: The revision addresses a documented issue and the repeated check shows whether it improved the assembly. items.title: Fusion-to-Mach3 CAM Workflow
items.description: Follow the approved workflow for creating Fusion toolpaths, posting a Mach3 .tap file, validating it in Mach3, and operating the DMC2 Mini.
items.searchText: Fusion-to-Mach3 CAM Workflow | LockwoodSTEM Skip to main content LockwoodSTEM Student Engineering Hub Menu Courses Daily Agenda Resources Certifications FabLab About Challenges Home Courses ADM Unit 4 Resource Center Fusion-to-Mach3 CAM Workflow ADM Unit 4 Resource Fusion-to-Mach3 CAM Workflow Follow the approved workflow for creating Fusion toolpaths, posting a Mach3 .tap file, validating it in Mach3, and operating the DMC2 Mini. Back to Unit 4 DMC2 Mini Workflow Fusion → Mach3 → CNC Use only the teacher-approved machine profile, post processor, files, tools, stock, and procedures. Required Safety Boundary A successful Fusion simulation or Mach3 toolpath display does not prove that a program is safe to run. Every new or revised setup requires teacher review, code verification, a workholding check, and an approved dry run before cutting. Digital thread Approved Production Workflow 1 Design in Fusion. Complete the approved component, technical drawing, material, tolerances, and revision. 2 Enter Manufacture. Create a Milling setup, select the model, define stock, and orient X/Y/Z to match the DMC2 Mini. 3 Define the origin. Select an accessible stock-box point or teacher-approved datum that can be established as the Mach3 work zero. 4 Select tools. Use only tools from the classroom Fusion library and verify diameter, flute length, holder, flute count, and tool number. 5 Create toolpaths. Use the assigned operations and approved speeds, feeds, stepdowns, stepovers, heights, and boundaries. 6 Simulate. Show tool, holder, stock, and toolpath. Inspect collisions, rapids, plunges, remaining stock, gouges, workholding clearance, and operation order. 7 Post process. Use the teacher-validated DMC2 Mini copy of Autodesk Mach3Mill. Post only approved operations and create the .tap file. 8 Inspect the code. Verify units, G90/G91 state, work offset, safe Z, minimum Z, feeds, speeds, spindle behavior, tool plan, and M30. 9 Load in Mach3. Use the approved DMC2 Mini Mach3 profile. Compare the toolpath display and extents with Fusion. 10 Set up the mill. Inspect tool, stock, workholding, axis condition, work zero, program, feed override, spindle method, and emergency stop. 11 Dry run. Complete the teacher-approved raised-Z, air-cut, or single-block verification. 12 Manufacture and inspect. Run under supervision, record interventions, inspect the component, and preserve traceability. Fusion setup checklist Before Simulation Correct Fusion design version Milling setup Correct model selected Approved stock dimensions X/Y/Z orientation matches mill Origin can be established physically G54/work-zero plan documented Classroom tool library used Heights and boundaries checked Clamps and fixture represented Mach3 checklist Before Cycle Start Correct DMC2 Mini Mach3 profile Correct .tap file and revision Units match Fusion Tool and stock match setup Work zero matches Fusion origin Toolpath extents reviewed Minimum Z and safe Z verified Spindle procedure confirmed Feed override set as directed Emergency stop accessible Dry run approved File traceability Record These Identifiers Fusion file and version Manufacture setup name Tool library revision Post processor name and revision NC program name .tap filename Mach3 profile Work offset Stock and tool Teacher approval date A student engineering hub for design, fabrication, and aerospace innovation. items.title: Mach3 G&M Code Reference
items.description: Interpret the teacher-approved Mach3 milling command subset used with the DMC2 Mini.
items.searchText: Mach3 G&M Code Reference | LockwoodSTEM Skip to main content LockwoodSTEM Student Engineering Hub Menu Courses Daily Agenda Resources Certifications FabLab About Challenges Home Courses ADM Unit 4 Resource Center Mach3 G&M Code Reference ADM Unit 4 Resource Mach3 G&M Code Reference Interpret the teacher-approved Mach3 milling command subset used with the DMC2 Mini. Back to Unit 4 DMC2 Mini Workflow Fusion → Mach3 → CNC Use only the teacher-approved machine profile, post processor, files, tools, stock, and procedures. Classroom Code Boundary This reference is for the teacher-approved DMC2 Mini Mach3 milling profile. A command may be supported by Mach3 but still be inappropriate for the classroom machine, tooling, spindle configuration, or current setup. Use only commands assigned by the teacher. Motion and coordinates Core G Codes G00 — rapid positioning; use only with verified clearance G01 — linear feed motion using F G02 / G03 — clockwise / counterclockwise circular interpolation when assigned G17 — XY plane G20 / G21 — inch / metric units G54 — teacher-approved work coordinate system G90 / G91 — absolute / incremental positioning G94 — feed per minute Machine states Safety and M Codes G40 — cancel cutter compensation G49 — cancel tool-length compensation when not used G80 — cancel canned cycle F — feed rate S — commanded spindle speed M03 — spindle clockwise only when the DMC2 Mini profile controls the spindle M05 — spindle stop only when configured M30 — program end and reset Instructional example Teacher-Reviewed Program Pattern (ADM U4 PRACTICE - NOT FOR MACHINE USE WITHOUT APPROVAL) G17 G21 G40 G49 G80 G90 G94 G54 G00 Z10.000 G00 X0.000 Y0.000 (M03 S____ only when configured and approved) G01 Z-1.000 F____ G01 X25.000 Y0.000 F____ G01 X25.000 Y15.000 G01 X0.000 Y15.000 G01 X0.000 Y0.000 G00 Z10.000 (M05 only when configured) M30 The numeric values are placeholders. Tool diameter, stock, origin, depth, feeds, speeds, and spindle behavior must come from the approved setup. Modal-state check Ask Before Every Run What units are active? Is positioning absolute or incremental? Which work offset is active? What plane is active? Are compensation and canned cycles canceled? What feed mode is active? Where is the tool now? What is the next Z movement? Mach3 file check Inspect the .tap File Correct program and revision Expected units Expected work offset Safe initial Z Correct minimum Z No unsupported commands Spindle behavior matches machine configuration Feeds and speeds approved Safe retract before rapid travel M30 at program end A student engineering hub for design, fabrication, and aerospace innovation.
